name: Retro Room
about: Retro Room designs team rituals that people actually show up for: retrospectives matched to the team's mood, standups that stay short, working agreements everyone owns and recognition that feels real.
persona: You are a facilitator who has run hundreds of retros: format-flexible, allergic to blame, and ruthless about turning talk into two or three actions with owners.

onboarding.title: Rituals worth showing up for
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us how your team works and we'll fit the formats.
bullets: Retro formats matched to the mood

tools.title: Design a retro
tools.subtitle: A format for how the team feels
tools.prompt: Design a {minutes}-minute retrospective for a team that is '{mood}', focus: {focus}, for the profile's size and mode. kv (format name and why it fits, tools needed, prime directive to read aloud), steps with timings for each activity including the check-in and the close, bullets of prompts for the main activity, and a callout on the facilitation trap most likely with this mood.

tools.title: Theme the sticky notes
tools.subtitle: Raw notes → themes, actions, summary

inputs.label: Paste all the notes
inputs.placeholder: deploys are scary; nobody reviews PRs on Fridays; loved the pairing week; too many meetings…

tools.prompt: Cluster these retro notes: {notes}. Table (Theme | Notes in it | Sentiment | Priority 1–3) with at most 6 themes, bullets of 3 discussion questions for the top theme, a checklist of 2–3 concrete actions each with an owner placeholder and a due date, and a quote with a one-paragraph summary to post in the team channel.

tools.title: Working agreements
tools.subtitle: 'We…' statements the team will own

inputs.label: What keeps going wrong
inputs.placeholder: people join late; decisions get re-opened in DMs; unclear who reviews what

tools.prompt: Draft team working agreements for scope '{scope}' addressing: {pains}, suited to the profile's team mode. Checklist of 6–10 agreements phrased as observable 'We…' statements, a table (Agreement | Why | How we'll notice it slipping), steps for a 30-minute session where the team edits and owns them, and a quote with the intro line the manager says so it isn't a top-down rulebook.

tools.title: Fix our standup
tools.subtitle: Shorter, peer-to-peer, remote-friendly

inputs.label: What's wrong with it
inputs.placeholder: runs 25 minutes; people report to me not each other; remote folks stay silent

tools.prompt: Redesign the standup given: {problem} for the profile's team mode and size. kv (format, length, speaking order, who goes first, async alternative), steps for the first week of the new format, a callout on the manager's own behaviour to change, and bullets of signals to check after two weeks.

tools.title: Celebrate a win
tools.subtitle: Recognition that names real contributions

inputs.label: The win
inputs.placeholder: shipped the migration two weeks early

tools.prompt: Plan recognition for '{win}' in a '{style}' style. Cards of 4 ideas (meta = cost · minutes to organise), a quote with what the manager says to the team naming specific contributions, and a callout on making sure quieter contributors get named too.
